history.heading: Rome
paragraphs: Italy was home to many ancient peoples, including the Etruscans in the centre and Greek colonies in the south (Magna Graecia). According to legend, Rome was founded in 753 BCE. It became a republic in 509 BCE and gradually conquered the Italian peninsula and the Mediterranean world.

After civil wars, Augustus became the first emperor in 27 BCE. The Roman Empire spread Latin, Roman law, roads and cities across Europe, North Africa and the Middle East. Christianity became the state religion in the 4th century, and Rome became the seat of the popes. The Western Roman Empire fell in 476.

history.heading: City-states and the Renaissance
paragraphs: After Rome's fall, Italy was divided among Ostrogoths, Byzantines, Lombards, Franks, Arabs in Sicily and Normans in the south. In the Middle Ages, wealthy city-states and maritime republics such as Venice, Genoa, Florence, Milan and Pisa flourished through trade and banking.

The Renaissance began in Italy in the 14th century. Artists and thinkers such as Dante, Petrarch, Leonardo da Vinci, Michelangelo, Raphael, Machiavelli and Galileo transformed art, literature and science, supported by patrons such as the Medici family of Florence. From the 16th century, much of Italy fell under Spanish and later Austrian control.

history.heading: Unification
paragraphs: The Risorgimento movement of the 19th century, led by figures such as Giuseppe Mazzini, Count Cavour and Giuseppe Garibaldi, unified Italy. The Kingdom of Italy was proclaimed in 1861, and Rome became the capital in 1871. Millions of Italians emigrated, especially to the Americas, in the following decades.

After the First World War, Benito Mussolini founded fascism and ruled as dictator from 1922. Italy allied with Nazi Germany in the Second World War. Mussolini was overthrown in 1943, and partisans fought German occupation until 1945.

history.heading: The Italian Republic
paragraphs: In 1946 Italians voted to abolish the monarchy and create a republic. Italy was a founding member of NATO and the European communities. The post-war "economic miracle" transformed it into an industrial power. The 1970s saw political terrorism, and the early 1990s the Mani Pulite corruption investigations that collapsed the old party system. Italy was hit hard early in the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020.

culture.heading: Art and heritage
paragraphs: Italy has more UNESCO World Heritage Sites than any other country, including the historic centres of Rome, Florence and Venice, Pompeii and the Amalfi Coast. Vatican City, an independent state, lies within Rome.

Italian is the official language, with many regional dialects and minority languages. Most Italians are Catholic. Italy has shaped Western music through opera, with Verdi, Puccini and Rossini, and has made major contributions to film, from Fellini to Sophia Loren.

culture.heading: Food and style
paragraphs: Italian cuisine is among the most popular in the world, with pasta, pizza, risotto, olive oil, cheeses such as Parmigiano-Reggiano, gelato and espresso, and strong regional traditions. Italy is one of the largest wine producers in the world.
Italy is a world leader in fashion and design, with Milan as a fashion capital and brands such as Gucci, Prada, Armani and Ferrari. Football is a passion; Italy has won the World Cup four times.

politics.heading: Parliamentary republic
paragraphs: Italy is a parliamentary republic. The prime minister (President of the Council of Ministers) leads the government, which needs the confidence of both chambers of parliament. The president, elected by parliament for seven years, is head of state and plays an important role in government crises.
Italian governments have historically been short-lived. In 2022 Giorgia Meloni of the right-wing Brothers of Italy became the first female prime minister, leading a stable right-wing coalition.

politics.heading: Italy in Europe
paragraphs: Italy is a founding member of the EU, a member of NATO and the G7, and has the third-largest economy in the eurozone. As a Mediterranean country, it is a main entry point for migrants arriving by sea from North Africa, a major political issue.

economy.heading: Industry and regions
paragraphs: Italy has a large, diversified economy with a strong manufacturing base, especially in the north. It is known for machinery, cars, fashion and luxury goods, food and wine, furniture and pharmaceuticals, often made by small and medium-sized family firms. Tourism is a major industry.
There is a long-standing gap between the more industrialised, wealthy north and the poorer south (the Mezzogiorno). The currency is the euro.

economy.heading: Challenges
paragraphs: Italy has had slow growth for decades, very high public debt, an ageing population with one of the lowest birth rates in Europe, emigration of young graduates and a large informal economy. EU recovery funds have financed a major investment programme since 2021.
